findings.title: The branch's deviations record still carries the retracted "40 comment lines - measured AT HEAD" figure; at HEAD it is 68, and the stated 1.5x ratio is 2.5x
findings.arbiter_reasoning: D1 reads, verbatim: "Measured at HEAD by first non-whitespace token, the production diff adds **27 code lines, 40 comment lines and 3 blank** - the reasoning is 1.5x the code". Re-derived at a40fe38d by the method the branch itself prescribes (`git diff 862a039d..HEAD -- src/lib/solicitation/ask-generation.ts`, classify each added line by its first non-whitespace token): 27 code, 68 comment, 3 blank. The code half is correct; the comment half is off by 28 lines and the ratio is 2.5x, not 1.5x. THE CLAIM IS EXPLICITLY SCOPED TO HEAD, so it is a false measurement rather than a dated one. It is also the branch's OWN already-adjudicated failure class, left half-fixed: triage T16 (triage.md:60) records this exact figure as P1 and marks it **FIXED**, and the arch-review-log row was duly rewritten to quote only the stable half plus the method ('THE COMMENT COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT QUOTED HERE - RE-DERIVE IT', arch-review-log.md:1555). The twin figure in D1 was never touched, so T16's FIXED overstates what was fixed, and the deviations doc now CONTRADICTS the arch-review-log row on the same branch: the row's durable claim is 'roughly two to three lines of recorded reasoning per line of code', D1 says 1.5x. The precedent is on the branch's own reading list: the #1080 arch row one entry above records 'The same 79 still stands, uncorrected, in `.feature/deviations.md` § D5' as a known residual. #1082 repeated the omission one ticket later and did not disclose it. SEVERITY: P1, not P0, matching how the identical claim was graded on this branch (RT1082-08). It misleads a later reader about a measurement, not about behaviour; no code, test or invariant is affected.

findings.title: The citation rule's new LIVING/DATED scope clause enumerates both buckets exhaustively and classifies the deviations doc into neither - which is where the stale figure of RT1082R3-01 survives
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The clause reads: LIVING = 'the plan, the intake, production comments, this file'; DATED = 'the four review reports and the red-team sidecar in this directory' plus 'every arch-review-log row this branch did not write'. Two documents this branch authored fall outside both lists: `docs/superpowers/plans/perf-1082-exhaustion-refusal-batch-deviations.md`, and the arch-review-log row this branch DID write (the clause exempts only rows it did not). THE SPLIT ITSELF IS COHERENT and I could not falsify it: the distinguishing test is whether a document asserts something about the CURRENT tree or records what was true at a measured SHA, and that test sorts the plan, the intake, the production comments and the triage file into LIVING and the four review reports into DATED correctly. Applying it to the deviations doc is what is missing, not the rule. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is reported rather than a style note: the audit the commit message claims ('Audited across every living document on this branch: zero line citations remain') is TRUE as far as it goes - I re-ran it and found zero `path:line` citations in the plan, both intake copies, the triage file, the production file and both test files, and confirmed the `:440-448` / `:579-587` occurrences in all four are narrative about the falsification, not citations. But the unclassified deviations doc was outside that sweep's stated scope and is exactly where RT1082R3-01 sits. An enumerated scope clause with a document missing from both buckets is how a half-fix passes an audit. P2: recorded, does not block. The remedy is one word - name the deviations doc (and the branch's own arch-review-log row) in the LIVING list.
